c.tagline: Golden pagodas rise above colonial streets and river haze.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered; negotiate fare before departure or use the Grab app for a fixed upfront price.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow; many hotels and tour operators keep direct lines to private clinics. Tourist Police available in central Yangon.

avoid.reason: Steer clear of any protest gatherings, military installations and checkpoints given post-2021 political instability, and skip the outlying industrial townships, which offer nothing for visitors and see more crime.
Street crime has risen since the coup, so take extra care after dark, during power cuts, and with bags around Bogyoke Market and busy downtown streets.

hood_desc: Colonial-era downtown grid around Sule Pagoda with crumbling heritage architecture, street markets, and budget-to-luxury hotels; best for first-time visitors who want to walk to major sights.
Dense, atmospheric Chinatown/Latha area famous for night food markets on 19th Street; suits budget travelers and foodies who don't mind noise and crowds.
Leafy, upscale residential area around Shwedagon Pagoda and Golden Valley with embassies and colonial mansions; suits travelers wanting quiet, greenery, and proximity to Myanmar's most sacred site.
Lakeside district around Kandawgyi (Royal) Lake with resort-style hotels, parks, and skyline views; good for mid-range/upscale travelers wanting a scenic, less chaotic base.
Quiet, leafy area around Inya Lake popular with diplomats and NGO staff, dotted with lakeside hotels and cafes; suits longer-stay visitors and those wanting calm over convenience.

water.note: Tap water isn't treated to safe standards; stick to bottled or boiled water and avoid ice from unknown sources.

transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash (small kyat notes) directly to the conductor on board; the circular train ticket is bought in cash at station windows. There is no unified transit card, so carry small MMK bills.
transit.hours: Buses and trains generally run approx. 5am-9pm; limited night options, most travelers use Grab or taxis after dark.
transit.note: YBS bus routes are extensive but signage is mostly in Burmese; the circular train is a scenic 3-hour loop popular with tourists rather than a fast commuter option.

train: Myanmar Railways intercity trains to Mandalay, Bagan, Bago
bus: Long-distance buses from Aung Mingalar and Dagon Ayeyar bus terminals
ferry: Dala Ferry across the Yangon River

transit.m: YBS airport shuttle bus (Yangon Airport Bus, ~45-60 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not traditionally expected but small tips for good service (guides, drivers, porters) are increasingly welcomed, especially in tourist-oriented businesses.
